To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cDNA encoding eIF-4 has been cloned, sequenced, and shown to contain the sequence encoding hypusine.
we sequenced eukaryotic translation initiation factor 4 (eIF- 4D) from rabbit reticulytes and cloned the cDNA from human HeLa cells.
the amino-terminal 50 amino acids of eIF-4 are modified by the unusual amino acid hypusine, and that this modification is essential for eIF-4 activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the eIF-4A and eIF-4B subunits, and the determination of the amino acid sequence and cDNA of the hypusine containing protein eIF-4G.
the molecular biology of protein synthesis.
eukaryotic protein synthesis and its regulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the human eIF-4F is identical to the rabbit protein.
eIF-4A is a 154-residue protein with an amino-terminal block and a single lysine residue modified to hypuine.
eIF-4-D is a 154-residue protein with a blocked N-terminus and a single hypusine residue at position 50.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have identified the cDNA for the protein that is the target for the post-translational modification that leads to the formation of hypusine, and we have determined the amino acid sequence of the protein.

the cDNA encodes the complete amino acid sequence of eIF-4A, that it contains a single open reading frame and that the amino acid sequence deduced from it is in complete agreement with the sequence of the protein as determined directly by chemical and enzymatic sequencing.
eIF-4-4D is a 17-kilodalton protein containing a single hypusine residue at Lys-50.
The main takeaway from our work is that
eIF-4 is a highly conserved protein.

the eIF-4A, eIF-4B, eIF-2 and eIF-3 proteins are all required for cap-dependent translation of globin mRNA in vitro, whereas the eIF-3 and eIF-4E proteins are not required for cap-independent translation of the same mRNA in the presence of poly(A) RNA.
eIF4D, the protein that contains hypusine, is an essential component of the translation initiation complex.
